evidence: The hunk shows `frag(failedConfigFile, ...)` with no sanitizeText while channelRows sanitizes every message line and the replaced openFileRow used sanitizeAndTruncate; the path derives from client-supplied project_dir, so control bytes could reach the terminal cell.
guidance_note: When a new render surface splices in a user-derived string, check how the code it replaces and its sibling surfaces sanitized that same string, and apply the same pass before the first review.

evidence: Only the path fragment is truncated via `Math.max(1, opts.width - fixedWidth)`, so the fixed head text overflows at narrow widths; the agent reproduced 40-41 cell rows at widths 1-24 and clipped the assembled row to width.
guidance_note: When a module documents an every-row-fits-width invariant, put narrow widths (1, 2, below the fixed text length) in the test table for every row kind, including the trailer.

evidence: sync's mkdirSync/writeFileSync were unguarded on the render path, so an fs error would turn a render that keeps a fallback bar into RENDER_FAILED; the fix returns a reason like writeLease. The reviewer also named reset()'s rmSync, which this fix did not cover (see F26).
guidance_note: When adding a best-effort fs side effect to a hot path, give every method of that owner (sync and reset) the codebase's existing non-throwing reason shape in the first commit.

evidence: The map does grow one short string per errored session until restart, but an eviction cap would have to delete a possibly-live session's file and leave its trailer linking a removed file, which the agent names; the growth is small and bounded by restarts.
Same defect as F3 at the call site: an unguarded diagnosticDump.sync would propagate out of handleRequest after body was already computed; fixed by logging the returned reason like writeLeaseFile.
guidance_note: Copy the codebase's established best-effort write pattern (writeLeaseFile's reason + dlog warn) when adding a new auxiliary write, rather than calling it bare.

evidence: Duplicate of F2: the fixed head text is never clipped and the row exceeds geometry.width at widths below ~40; the same whole-row truncation fixed both.

CLAUDE.md said the trailer always links the failing config file, but trailerRow emits that link only when failedConfigFile !== null, which the PR's own test 'without a failed config file the trailer offers only the full text' pins.
guidance_note: When documenting a composed output, write each part's condition from the code's branches (and the tests that pin them), not from the common case.

evidence: An abandoned run can write stale text late, but it also records that text in `written`, so the next render's compare sees a difference and rewrites; the stale window is one render tick on a status line that re-renders constantly, which is not worth a sequence-number owner.

The scenario needs an outside writer in a single-owner directory, and an existing test pins the no-recheck behaviour; an existsSync per render guards a broken contract. F13 later found a real in-codebase case (a losing daemon's reset), and it was fixed at that cause, not with this guard.
TS parseInt accepts ' 80', '80.5', '80\n' while Rust str::parse::<u32> rejects them, and this PR extended the helper to LINES; the agent made TS match Rust's grammar exactly.
guidance_note: When extracting a helper that both runtimes mirror, pin the shared accept/reject table in tests on both sides in the same commit.

evidence: Input lines really are processed without a bound, but the elision count is the row count of the full fold, so an input cap would make 'N more rows' wrong or need a second wrap algorithm; the cost is linear in the config author's own error text.

docs/render-path-subprocess-accounting.md's call-chain diagram listed no disk write, while the PR's original diff added a synchronous diagnosticDump.sync to that chain; the sync call predates every fix, so this is an original-PR doc omission.
guidance_note: When adding a step to a hot path, grep for docs that enumerate that path's call chain and update them in the same commit.

evidence: The hunk shows the original PR placing diagnosticDump.reset() in runDaemon before bind arbitration, while every other daemon-identity effect runs in onListening; a losing process would rm -rf the winner's live dump directory.
guidance_note: When adding a daemon-start side effect, place it beside the existing post-bind-win effects in onListening rather than in pre-bind bootstrap.

evidence: The dump is verbatim by design and sanitizeText would collapse its line structure; the control bytes come from the user's own config file, which the neighbouring link already opens, so the extra exposure is marginal.

The F3/F5 fix made sync return a failure reason but left `fullTextFile: diagnosticDump.pathFor(sessionId)` baked into Diagnostics before the write, so a failed write still rendered a working-looking link; before that fix the render failed outright and showed no link.
guidance_note: When turning a throw into a returned failure, trace every value built before the effect that assumes it succeeded, and derive those values from the outcome in the same commit.

evidence: The F10 fix rewrote detectTermExtent to /^\+?\d+$/ to match Rust, but the function was unexported in src/index.ts and no test on either side pinned the parity it claimed.
guidance_note: A fix that claims cross-runtime parity ships the shared accept/reject table as tests on both runtimes in the same commit.

evidence: The original-PR hunk inserts termRows as another member but leaves 'keeps that third addition a field', which now miscounts.
guidance_note: When adding a member to a list a comment describes, reread the whole comment for counts and ordinals that the addition invalidates.

evidence: Same defect as F15; the reviewer says it directly: 'the fix that made sync non-throwing didn't also make the trailer conditional on that outcome.'
guidance_note: When turning a throw into a returned failure, make every downstream affordance that names the effect's result conditional on that outcome.

evidence: Third report of F15: the link is built before the now-non-throwing sync runs, so a refused write still renders a clickable link to a file that does not exist.

encodeURIComponent throws URIError on a lone surrogate, and validateHookData only checked typeof string, so a malformed session_id failed every render; pathFor was eager in the original PR. The chosen cure (inland toWellFormed) was one of the reviewer's two options and caused the F25 collision.
guidance_note: When hook input can make an inland encoder throw, tighten the border validator so the input is rejected there, rather than normalizing it at the call site.

evidence: The write is synchronous on the event loop, but `written` limits it to changes in diagnostic text, it is a few KB, and async writes would reopen the per-session ordering race that F8 raised.

The reviewer itself could not verify whether rich-js coalesces same-style cells; the agent reports a measurement (19 OSC-8 opens for 19 rows) and cites rich-js Style docs, but the packet contains neither the measurement nor the docs.
The F13 fix moved diagnosticDump.reset() into onListening but left the declaration comment saying 'the daemon wipes it in runDaemon() (reset)'.
guidance_note: When moving a call, grep for comments that name its old location (here 'runDaemon() (reset)') and update them in the same commit.

evidence: The F15 fix added a `full text unavailable: <reason>` unlinked variant, but CLAUDE.md:222 and :65 still described the complete-text link as unconditional.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a new variant to a rendered output, search the docs for every sentence that describes that output and add the new condition.

evidence: The F20 fix's `encodeURIComponent(sessionId.toWellFormed())` maps every lone surrogate to U+FFFD, so distinct ids collide on %EF%BF%BD.txt (its own test pinned that basename). The agent rejected the hash-suffix cure and moved the well-formedness check into validateHookData.
guidance_note: Before normalizing an input to make an encoder total, check whether the normalization is injective; if it is not, reject the input at the border.

evidence: F3 explicitly asked to wrap 'the reset()/rmSync calls' too, but the fix changed only sync; reset's rmSync still threw out of onListening into uncaughtException → shutdown(1). Commit adb20cb shows reset gaining the same string|null shape.
guidance_note: When a finding names several call sites, close it only after every named site is changed; read the finding's full list before marking it fixed.

evidence: collectDiagnostics pushed a channel on `!== null` while channelRows filtered sanitized-empty lines, so a whitespace-only message produced a trailer-only strip; both pieces are original-PR code. adb20cb moves line derivation into channelOf with a non-empty tuple type.
guidance_note: When a type comment claims 'non-empty by construction', make the constructor derive the thing that is claimed non-empty (here the rendered lines), not a proxy for it.

evidence: The missing wide-glyph trailer test was real, but the reviewer called the overflow 'unverified'; the agent measured RichText.truncate as bounded and added the test over widths 25-60 (visible in adb20cb) instead of the floor change. The truncate call is original-PR code; the F2 fix only prompted the analogy.
guidance_note: When a fix uncovers a library edge case at one call site (chopCells below 2 cells), test the same edge case at every other call site of that library family in the same commit.

evidence: The per-render dlog warn was added by the F5 fix. Logging every render under a persistent failure is real churn, but the agent shows that other per-request failures in this file also log unthrottled, and dedup would add a second per-session map just to tidy logs.

The F16 fix (3baf0c2) moved detectTermExtent to src/term-extent.ts but left the Rust comment at main.rs:395 saying 'src/index.ts'. adb20cb does not touch main.rs; the drift comes from the earlier move.
guidance_note: When moving a function, grep both runtimes for its name to update cross-language 'Mirrors X in <file>' comments.

evidence: pathFor does run on every render inside the links value the F15 fix built, and the agent's own F20 reply had claimed it is 'only reached when a diagnostic exists'. Since adb20cb it is a pure path.join that cannot throw, so a gate would add a branch only to save the join.
guidance_note: Don't state an invariant in a fix reply ('only reached when a diagnostic exists') without checking that the code makes it true.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: the stale 'Current categories (11)' list predates this PR and no fix touched it; the reviewer only reached it because the F12 fix edited the same doc. The agent confirmed LAUNCH_CATEGORIES has 13 entries.

The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: the nonexistent `renderDslLine` name was already in the diagram line (context, not added) above the F12 fix's new line; the agent confirmed zero hits outside the doc.
guidance_note: When adding a line to a call-chain diagram, verify each neighbouring name in the diagram against the code with a grep.

evidence: adb20cb's kindOf applies well-formedness to every required string field, which is the F25 fix's scope. The reviewer's harm case needs real paths to carry lone surrogates; on darwin/linux, Node decodes invalid filename bytes to U+FFFD, and BAD_REQUEST renders an error glyph naming the field rather than a blank bar, per the agent's reply.

narrative: A large feature PR (diagnostic strip, dump file, termRows hint) drew 11 findings in round 0, mostly real original-PR defects that were fixed well. The fixes then generated a chain of follow-ups: making sync non-throwing left the link built before the write (F15/F18/F19), and the reset half of the same request went unfixed until round 3 (F26). Inland toWellFormed traded a throw for a path collision (F25), and two fixes moved code without updating the comments and docs that named it (F23, F24, F30). Round 2 was entirely fix-caused doc/comment drift. The agent's pushbacks (F4, F8, F9, F11, F14, F21, F29, F31, F34) were mostly well-reasoned and held.
guidance_observations: Several fixes addressed only the first call site a finding named (sync but not reset), so read the whole finding before declaring it fixed.

Each fix that moved or renamed code (reset into onListening, detectTermExtent into term-extent.ts, the new unavailable-link variant) cost a later round for stale comments or docs; a grep for the old name or location after each move would have prevented them.
The first cure for a hostile-input throw normalized the input inland instead of rejecting it at the border, which cost a round and then a scope argument (F25, F34).

evidence: drawShapes returned a prebuilt rng closure per shape that four separate test blocks drew from, so an isolated run replays different draws than a full run; 0ebdbd9 makes each test call seededRng(seed) locally.
guidance_note: When a test file promises reproducibility from a seed, give each test its own seeded generator instead of sharing mutable rng state across test blocks.

evidence: The new paragraph called decorFor the replacement for hue.step, while the very next paragraph said authored shiftHue config was 'the direction any replacement should take'; 0ebdbd9 rewrote that clause. The reply-hint says pushback, but the reply is 'Plan: valid' and was implemented.
guidance_note: When adding a doc paragraph about a topic, reread the adjacent paragraphs on the same topic and the design doc it links, and reconcile every claim before pushing.

evidence: The F2 fix (0ebdbd9) edited only the tail of the paragraph and kept the opening 'hue.step is **not** load-bearing' claim, which the PR's own design doc calls 'wrong twice over'; dae0089 rewrote the paragraph.
guidance_note: When fixing one stale clause in a paragraph, check the paragraph's remaining claims against the authority you are reconciling to (here the linked design doc) before pushing.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: the literal 18 is original-PR code, and 0ebdbd9 changed only the rng lines. The reviewer's cure (DECOR_VOCABULARY.length) would still fail confusingly because 5 is correct only at size 18, so the agent asserted the size premise explicitly.
guidance_note: When a test pins a value that depends on a size, assert that size as a named premise next to the pinned value.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: dae0089 does not touch decor.ts, and AddressStep is original code. The reviewer concedes no harm today; the producer reads index and count from one children array, and n-free distributions never read count, so an inland guard would be a second enforcer.

If the drawn permutation target is the root, isUnder([], path) skips every non-root node, so the draw checks only the root and is vacuous. The F1 fix touched these lines only to add seededRng; the root-eligible filter is unchanged original code, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: For a property test of the form 'X outside the mutated region is unchanged', exclude draws whose outside region is empty, or assert that it is non-empty.

evidence: CLAUDE.md called decorFor 'the pure replacement for hue.step' while the design doc's Decisions section says hue.step is 'removed with no successor'. The F2/F3 fixes treated the design doc as the authority for one paragraph without sweeping CLAUDE.md for its other contradictions, and dae0089's 'deletes it in favour of decorFor' restated the same claim.
guidance_note: When a fix declares one document the authority, diff every claim in the other document against it in the same pass, not just the sentence the reviewer quoted.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive: the vocabularyIndex export is original code. A direct caller with size 0 does get NaN, but the only real caller (vocabularySelect) already throws; un-exporting removes the unenforced public seam without adding a guard.
guidance_note: Export only the seam callers need; a helper whose precondition is enforced by its one caller should stay module-private.

evidence: vocabularySelect<T> treated `entry === undefined` as 'empty vocabulary', which misreports for any T that includes undefined; the agent took the reviewer's second option, `T extends {}`. The code is original, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When a generic function uses undefined as a sentinel, constrain T to exclude undefined in the signature.

evidence: The design doc added by this PR says hueUp/hueDown exist only as a CLAUDE.md illustration, while CLAUDE.md's example says it 'mirrors the maintainer's live config'. This is another unswept CLAUDE.md-vs-design-doc contradiction of the kind F2/F3 fixed one sentence at a time.
guidance_note: When adding a design doc that makes factual claims about existing docs, grep the existing docs for each claimed fact (here hueUp/hueDown) and reconcile them before the first review.

narrative: A small pure-module PR (decorFor plus property tests) whose code findings (F1, F4, F5, F6, F8, F9) were all original-PR issues, handled with judgment, including two good different fixes (DEMO_SIZE premise, un-exporting vocabularyIndex). The avoidable cost was documentation: the PR added a design doc that contradicted CLAUDE.md in several places, and each fix reconciled only the sentence the reviewer quoted, so F3, F7 and F10 arrived one round at a time. Round 3 came back clean. Since code findings also drove rounds 1 and 2, no round was purely avoidable.
guidance_observations: When a PR adds a design doc, diff its factual claims against CLAUDE.md before the first push; three of ten findings were contradictions between those two files.
Fixes for doc contradictions edited the quoted sentence instead of reconciling the whole topic, so each round surfaced the next sentence.
